d: Tool balancing made easy Imbalances in your tool quickly become a problem in several respects: They run out of round, put a strain on the spindle and machine, impair the cutting pe
x: tool balancing made easy imbalances in your tool quickly become a problem in several respects: they run out of round, put a strain on the spindle and machine, impair the cutting performance and ultimately your entire process reliability. top what are the consequences of the imbalance in the tool? tools that run unevenly cannot be used with the same precision that you need for your work over the long term. the vibrations that occur not only reduce the overall cutting performance, they also create artifacts on the workpieces, such as chatter marks, which may have to be reworked. imbalances in the tool therefore lead to very specific quality losses and jeopardize the process reliability of your processes. in addition, imbalances also reduce the service life of the spindle and possibly the machine - the costs for this quickly exceed the expenses incurred by frequent balancing of the tools. top what does unbalance mean? the term "unbalance" is used to describe the ubiquitous phenomenon in rotating bodies that their mass is not distributed over the body in a rotationally symmetrical manner. there are three main types of unbalance: static unbalance: here, the center of gravity of the rotating body lies outside the axis of rotation. this can already be measured at standstill. torque unbalance: the center of gravity is on the axis of rotation; the unbalance only becomes measurable during the rotary motion. dynamic unbalance: the term dynamic unbalance combines the two other forms of unbalance, in any combination of static unbalance and torque unbalance. this is the rule for technical rotors. each specific form of unbalance can be corrected by making appropriate adjustments to the rotating body. during rotation, the greater the unbalance (linear growth) and the faster the rotational movement (quadratic growth), the more noticeable the unbalance becomes. the faster the rotational movement, the more important balancing becomes and the more important it is to reduce the residual unbalance as much as possible. balancing should therefore be systematically integrated into the work process. top what causes imbalances in tool operation? imbalances are a well-known and regularly occurring phenomenon in rotating tool systems. there are various possible causes, for example: a tool consisting of several individual parts was not assembled correctly - for example, if the tool holder and the tool are not exactly aligned and deviate from the axis of rotation. the mass distribution

x: balancing the grinding wheel? with our balancing system »toolbalancer«, it's child's play our balancing system increases tool life finely balanced tools are extremely important for modern cutting machines. unbalances in grinding wheels, tool systems, and rotors cause wear and tear or even damage—regular balancing prevents downtime and reduces your costs. top efficient balancing with the zoller »toolbalancer« long balancing times cause downtime and loss of quality. with our »toolbalancer«, not only can tool-holding fixtures, grinding wheels, and rotors be balanced with high precision—its automated measurement sequence also significantly speeds up the process. your current requirements can be taken into account, as well as developments that you cannot yet assess: thanks to its modular design, the »toolbalancer« can be adjusted/adapted to suit your individual needs. the tool balancing machine can be used intuitively and self-explanatorily via touchscreen, keyboard, or mouse—whichever suits your working style best. this allows you to concentrate on working and producing effectively, to a high standard of quality. you can measurably reduce your scrap rates, machine downtime, and production costs! more about »toolbalancer« center higher cutting performance longer tool life better component quality what is balancing? balancing reduces or, ideally, corrects existing unbalances that occur in any rigid body that is rotating around a fixed axis. the unbalances are caused by uneven mass distribution in the grinding wheel; the reference point in each case is the axis of rotation of the grinding spindle. the main goal of balancing is to perform correction for all centrifugal forces acting on the rotating spindle so that the spindle bearing is not subjected to any additional forces. top how do unbalances arise in grinding wheels? unbalances in a grinding wheel can already occur during manufacture, for example: slight deviations from the ideal geometric shape or a perfectly symmetrical shape due to production errors. other manufacturing errors, or uneven density of the grinding wheel structure (resulting in uneven weight distribution). however, unbalances are primarily caused by wear and tear during the grinding process. examples of this are: uneven abrasion during the grinding process, pollution by chips or coolants or lubricants, and stress and deformation due to clamping forces, cutting forces, and centrifugal forces. additional problems can arise from improper storage

t: How to Deal with the Tungsten Price Shock
d: There are two strategies to counter the extreme price increases for solid carbide tools: greater efficiency in tool usage and the highest precision in regrinding processes.
x: 2026-06-22 06/22/2026 press release tool management solid carbide tools: how to cope with the tungsten price shock there are two strategies to counter the extreme price increases for solid carbide tools: greater efficiency in tool usage and the highest precision in regrinding processes. zoller offers the right solutions for both: measuring technology, inspection technology, and digital tool management. anyone currently ordering solid carbide tools in germany is rubbing their eyes in disbelief. while uncoated carbide rods were called up at around 30 euros per kilogram in october 2025, the price settled between 200 and 240 euros per kilogram in may 2026 – an 800 percent price increase in seven months. other markets were also hit hard, with price increases ranging from 300 to 500 percent. top top tungsten – key raw material sees rising prices the price driver is well known: the element tungsten. tungsten is indispensable for solid carbide tools, not least because of its melting point of 3,422 °c – no other element can withstand higher temperatures. in tools, tungsten occurs as tungsten carbide. the key indicator in international pricing is the intermediate product ammonium paratungstate (apt). in october 2025, the price stood at around 580 euros per ten kilograms (which corresponds to one metric ton unit, mtu). by early june 2026, it had skyrocketed to around 2,560 euros. according to experts, the price situation is unlikely to change much in the medium term. china is the main supplier. eighty percent of tungsten deposits and the majority of the management. anyone currently ordering solid carbide tools in germany is rubbing their eyes in disbelief. while uncoated carbide rods were called up at around 30 euros per kilogram in october 2025, the percent. top top tungsten – key raw material sees rising prices the price driver is well known: the element tungsten. tungsten is indispensable for solid carbide tools, not least because of its melting point of 3,422 °c – no other element can withstand higher temperatures. in tools, tungsten occurs as tungsten carbide. the key indicator in international pricing is the intermediate product ammonium paratungstate (apt). in october 2025, the price stood at around 580 euros per ten kilograms (which corresponds to one metric ton unit, mtu). by early june 2026, it had skyrocketed to around 2,560 euros. according to experts, the price situation is unlikely to change much in the medium term. china is the main supplier. eighty percent of tungsten deposits and the majority of the infrastructure used to process tungsten are located there. in early 2026, the resource giant restricted tungsten exports, triggering alarm bells on the global market. limited recycling potential there d: Greater precision Measuring and testing devices are just as important as the associated software. In order for tools to do exactly what they were designed and constructed for, they
x: greater precision measuring and testing devices are just as important as the associated software. in order for tools to do exactly what they were designed and constructed for, they must themselves be manufactured with precision. with our universal measuring machines, tools can be measured with micrometer accuracy and checked to ensure they correspond to the requirements. top measuring in the coordinate measuring system the measured probe points are assigned by the measuring machines to a specific length measuring system along a specific traverse axis. the measuring software then processes this information and assigns it to specific points in the entire coordinate measuring system. the cmm software then uses the coordinates determined in this way to calculate the values for quantities that are not measured directly, such as lengths, angles, distances between two measuring points, etc. the measuring points (actual values) determined in the coordinate measuring system are then compared with the values resulting from the specifications, such as the designs for the tool (nominal values). if these do not accord, i.e., if there are measurement deviations – whether due to production errors or wear and tear – appropriate action can then be taken. what are 3d measuring machines ? "3d measuring machines" are usually measuring machines that can measure the three-dimensional dimensions of a measurement object in a relatively short time, ideally in real time. when compact linear or matrix array cameras are used, some of these testing machines can even be portable or at least transportable. however, portable cmms are generally somewhat less accurate than conventional testing machines. center coordinate measuring technology many measuring machines work with what is known as coordinate measuring technology. the measuring machine (the full designation is then "coordinate measuring machine," cmm) uses a suitable sensor to enter the exact coordinates at which certain points are located on the surface of the workpiece. in most cases, the coordinate system is created parallel to the orthogonal traverse axes of the coordinate measuring systems. non-contact probing non-contact probing, on the other hand, uses cameras, laser triangulation sensors, and other methods, such as optical or electrical sensors. in this case, the measuring process takes place without the measuring sensor coming into contact with the workpiece at all. under certain circumstances, this can significantly spe

tool not only prevents typing errors and other transmission problems, it is also completed in a very short time. this not only reduces setup time to a minimum, but also means that the setup time for the new tool is effectively zero – allowing you to maximize tool life. top preset device – the advantages setup time and setup time are separated: tools can be prepared while the cnc machine tool is still running—this can even take place in separate locations if this facilitates or speeds up the work processes. no setup time: electronic transmission of the prepared tool data ensures that the transfer directly from the presetting device to the cnc machine. quality from the very first part: your machines, perfectly supplied with data, produce top results and no rejects from the very first workpiece. with exact measurements of tools, there are also no crashes or interruptions. longer tool life: minimized setup and adjustment times allow the machine to work more effectively and x: »robomark« übersicht applications software & integration faq 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top which pallet systems are supported? the »robomark« automation solution is designed to be flexible and can be operated with different pallet systems. top do existing systems need to be adjusted? no. »robomark« is designed to integrate into existing manufacturing environments. in many cases, existing systems can continue to be used while tool data is automatically provided and processed. this keeps the integration effort low, and existing processes can continue to run largely unchanged. top is it possible to trace the tools? yes, if questions arise regarding tools or if quality documentation is needed, the relevant information is readily available. thanks to permanent labeling and automatic documentation, tools can be uniquely identified and assigned. this saves time when searching for data and ensures greater safety in production. top what happens if the tool has internal cooling? tools with internal cooling can be labeled with »robomark« without any problems. laser labeling is applied to the circumference of the shank and does not affect the function of the cooling channels. the labeling position is selected to ensure safe and permanent labeling while maintaining unobstructed tool functionality. top can weldon tools be labeled? d: FAQ - »hobCheck« – FAQ
x: »hobcheck« übersicht features software & integration options & accessories technical data faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top which tools can i measure with the zoller »hobcheck«? the universal »hobcheck« measuring machine can measure and set a wide range of tools such as hobs, taps, end mills, step drills and forming tools. top which gear cutting tools can i measure with the »hobcheck«? the »hobcheck« offers very accurate measurements that are carried out in accordance with the relevant standards such as din 3968 and din 1829. top how long does the complete measurement of a tool take? a complete measurement of a hob according to din 3968 usually only takes a few minutes. the data creation for a new tool is required only once and is also very quick. top what advantages does the integrated probe offer? the measuring probe makes it possible to measure parameters that remain hidden to the camera, such as the rake angle, the pitch and the flute direction. this is particularly interesting for resharpeners. top how are the measurement results evaluated? the measurement results are automatically evaluated in accordance with the relevant standards and a specific report with graphics is created. top how does automation work with the »hobcheck«? the »hobcheck« can be used in combination with the »roboset 2« automation solution. this allows tools to be loaded, measured, sorted and documented fully automatically - around the clock and without an operator. top what interfaces does the zoller »hobcheck« offer? the »hobcheck« has open data interfaces to transfer measurement data directly to cad/cam systems, grinding machines and tool management software. this allows processes to be digitalized end-to-end. top how are the measurement results documented? all measurement results are documented in detail and can be passed on to customers as test reports. this means that the quality of the tools can be fully verified. top what advantages does the »hobcheck« offer for grinding shops? for grinding shops, the »hobcheck« enables fully automatic and precise measurement of grinding wheels. this reduces set-up costs and optimizes tool life. top how is the »hobcheck« integrated into production? »hobcheck« can be integrated directly into the production processes. this allows tool data to be transferred from cad/cam systems and target/actual comparisons to be used for optimized grinding process control. top inspection & measuring: your advantages inspection & measuri

d: FAQ - »genius« – FAQ
x: »genius« übersicht features software & integration options & accessories technical data faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top what is the main difference between setting tools and inspection tools? additional axes, sensors and cameras are available on inspection devices in order to be able to fully measure cutting tools. top which tools are measured on the zoller machines? all rotary cutting tools can be measured on the zoller inspection machines. in addition, stationary tools such as indexable inserts can be easily measured according to customer requirements using our special adapters. top can i connect the inspection devices to a grinding machine? absolutely, through the network connection or with a usb stick you can transfer the tool file from measuring devices to the grinding machine, or vice versa. for example, we offer a file interface for many programming systems. top do i need a lot of time to measure standard tools? no, our software contains an automatically created program, the zoller »elephant«. with this program, you can easily measure the basic geometries without many settings. top what is the difference between »genius« and »threadcheck«? zoller »threadcheck« is based on the »genius« structure, but has an additional axis for horizontal swiveling and several special programs for measuring threading tools. the swivel allows the contour of the thread flanks to be correctly focused and measured without distortion. top can i only measure tools on the inspection devices? no, you can measure various objects, e.g. grinding wheels or the finished workpiece. top how extensive can the tools be in order to successfully measure them on the zoller machines? our inspection devices can be equipped with different cameras at the customer's request. for tool manufacturers, who mostly produce tools larger than 3 mm in diameter, we recommend the standard camera for macro tools. for micro tool manufacturers, we recommend a micro camera for tools with a diameter from 0.4 mm. top can beginners also quickly mix tools on the inspection devices? yes, we can save the measured tools in our z.one database and call them up again at any time. this means that even operators with little experience can call up the saved programs independently. the tool is measured exactly as specified. top is an air-conditioned room required for the installation? an air-conditioned room is not required. the device can be installed in a dust-free area in the machine hall. top a

x: »powershrink« übersicht models features options & accessories technical specifications faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top what temperature is the tool holder heated to during the shrinking process? this depends on the geometry of the holder, the size of the clamping diameter and the taper size. while some standard holders have 4.5 degrees, slim holders have 3 degrees. depending on the type, a different temperature from 150˚c to 350˚c is used when shrinking the holder. top what types of cutting materials can be used in shrink-fit holders for the shrink-fit process? steel, hss, carbide, heavy metals, metal powder, shrink-fit extensions. top what is the required tolerance for the shank diameter of the cutting tool when using a shrink-fit tool holder? the shank tolerance of the cutting tool must be h6 or h5. top is it possible to monitor the service life of the tool holder and the number of shrink cycles of the tool holder? with the zoller »powershrink« it is possible to monitor the heating cycles of the tool holder using a unique tool holder id number, e.g. the zoller »idchip« technology. each cycle is monitored and registered in the »pilot« software. top what is the minimum and maximum heating time? the heating time depends on the geometry of the tool holder and the clamping diameter. for small diameters, this takes 2 to 3 seconds, for large diameters 5 to 7 seconds. top what is the minimum and maximum cooling time? zoller offers two types of cooling systems: a non-contact cooling system with air cooling and cooling adapters. depending on the tool diameter, the cooling time with cooling adapters is 60 to 120 seconds. with »zstream« air cooling, the process is called conditioning, in which the entire tool holder is cooled from the nose to the flange. the conditioning time here depends on the diameter of the holder and is 3 to 5 minutes. top is an air-conditioned room required to install the »powershrink« device? we have developed a special shrink-fit function for this purpose, whereby the broken-off shank tool is pushed out using the »asza« automatic length stop system. top can i also shrink mst shrink fit holders with the »redomatic«? the zoller »redomatic 600« mst was specially developed for the automated measuring, setting and shrinking of shank tools in mst shrink fit chucks. top how often can i shrink my shrink fit holder until it is worn out? the service life depends on the manufacturer and can be specified in our database. our zoller coil heats your lining extremely gently to get the maximum service life out of it and reduces your energy costs by up to 30 %. top how precisely can i shrink and measure with the »redomatic«? once you have inserted the shrink fit chuck, the »masterpiece« setting adapter and the tool into the »redomatic«, the length stop is automatically set to match the target tool length. this gives you an accuracy of less than 10 μm when setting the target length. the measuring repeatability of the »redomatic« is the same as that of other zoller presetting and measuring machines and is max. 2 μm. top what coil options are available? x: übersicht faq info pool 33-66 faq frequently asked questions top what is webtms? zoller webtms tool management solutions is the web version of the desktop application tms, which can be used on various devices. as webtms has been developed from scratch, not all modules and functions of the tms desktop version are currently available. advantages of a web application: no installation on devices required. any device with a browser (pc, smartphone, tablet, notebook, etc.) can access webtms immediately. installation, configuration and maintenance only take place on the host device, which significantly reduces the administrative effort. top what is the webtms startup edition? the webtms startup edition is the first version of webtms to be launched on the market. it is pre-installed on all setting and measuring devices as well as tms hardware products»(keeper«, »autolock«, »toolorganizer«, »ztower«, »toolstation«, »cockpit«) so that customers can get started immediately. as soon as the device is connected to the network, simply start webtms. from this point on, the software can be used on any device with a browser without any additional installation. top can the webtms startup edition also be used by tms customers? this version of webtms is not compatible with tms as it is hosted on the ipc of the presetting and measuring machine or a tms hardware product that is not designed for this dual use. the simultaneous use of both systems can lead to performance problems and crashes. a compatible on-premise version (beta phase), which is installed and hosted on a customer's server, is currently under development. top how do i install or set up webtms? no installation is required as webtms is already pre-installed on the setting and measuring device or a tms hardware product. all you need to do is create a test license (or select a purchased license) and start webtms on the device that is to act as the host. optionally, the database, graphics and document path can be configured. to enable access from other devices, the setting and measuring device or a tms hardware product must be integrated into the network. access is via the standard ports 80 and 443. top how can a customer purchase or extend a license? d: Why optimize setup time? Nowadays, almost no machine or system manufactures just one product—as a rule, they are converted for different products as required. This results in setup
x: why optimize setup time? nowadays, almost no machine or system manufactures just one product—as a rule, they are converted for different products as required. this results in setup times during which the machine usually produces nothing. top what does setup time mean? setup time is the period during which the machine or system is converted from manufacturing one product to another. if, for example, piece goods are manufactured, setup time is defined as the time from the last good part of the old batch to the first good part of the new batch. setup time is therefore not "waste" in the actual sense of the word, but since it means at least partial machine downtime, longer setup times naturally reduce the productivity and effectiveness of your production facilities. center 33-66 how can i optimize setup time? optimizing setup time means above all: minimizing setup time! there are various approaches to achieving this goal. top analyze setup processes every improvement process aimed at reducing setup time is preceded by an analysis of the setup procedures: which steps are necessary? which ones are currently being performed, and how much time does this take? in what order are the steps performed, and can this be changed? which steps are really necessary, and which ones can be optimized? top optimize batch sizes a thorough analysis also includes the question: is it possible to retool the systems less frequently overall, i.e., to reduce the number of product changes? less frequent changeovers are naturally less time-consuming and therefore save money. at the same time, the costs saved as a result must be clearly weighed against the desire to keep inventory as low as possible, i.e., to avoid overproduction of goods. and, of course, plant utilization should remain as high as possible throughout all of this. top external setup when it comes to setup time, a distinction is made between external setup (activities that are also possible while the production system is running) and internal setup (which requires the system to be shut down). it is naturally in your interest to keep internal setup, which forces productivity losses, as short as possible. top digitization and automation with modern machines, the thorough digitization and automation of setup processes is a crucial measure. tool presetters, for example, can determine the necessary tool data for a cnc machine tool in advance, i.e., measure tools and make the correct settings directly. this dramatically reduces in

t: Increasing tool life – Tips and Solutions
d: Increase the tool life of your tools 50-50 How to extend the lifetime of your cutting tools top The longer the tool life of a cutting tool, the lower the cost of that tool and the
x: increase the tool life of your tools 50-50 how to extend the lifetime of your cutting tools top the longer the tool life of a cutting tool, the lower the cost of that tool and the more effectively it can work. so what is the best way to increase tool life? from a purely linguistic point of view, the term "tool life" for cutting tools seems a little counterintuitive. this is because it does not describe the time during which a tool stands around uselessly, but rather the exact opposite: tool life describes the total time during which a cutting tool is in use (i.e., actually performing material removal) before it needs to be exchanged. the time required to exchange the workpiece is therefore not included in the tool life. replacing a tool, in turn, incurs costs in several ways: a new tool must be purchased and used, and the old one must be reground or disposed of. it takes working time to remove the old tool (and regrind it later, if necessary) and insert a new one. while the tool is being exchanged, the machine is idle and the production process is at a standstill – the more frequently an exchange is required, the more production losses there are. you have increased storage and procurement costs for your tool inventory. longer tool life therefore means less machine downtime and thus enables more effective work overall, reducing your production costs. new tool purchases can be avoided by regrinding the tools. regrinding the tool cutting edges significantly extends the lifetime of the cutting tool and thus saves on the cost of purchasing new tools. the »edgecontrol« measuring machine is helpful here. the device detects the greatest amount of wear and tear on a cutting edge. this allows the tool to be reground only as much as is actually necessary, with an accuracy of µm. learn more about wear marks and defects along the cutting edge top 50-50 what affects tool life? top there are simple physical reasons why the tool life is limited: machining causes wear and tear on the tool, as the material it is made of is subjected to mechanical stress and also heated. this logically leads to the most important factors that influence tool life: the tool geometry, i.e., the specific shape of the tool, the material from which the tool is made, the specific machining conditions (in particular cutting speed, feed, and cutting depth), the material from which the workpiece is made (the workpiece or cutting material), and the temperature or changes in the temperature of the tool.

x: quick tool change with shrink unit with a good shrink-fit device, tool changes can be carried out quickly, easily and reliably with different tool holders. we describe how this works and the benefits in more detail here. top what happens during tool shrinking? shrinking the tool does not mean that the size of the tool itself is reduced. instead, the tool holder into which a drilling or cutting tool is inserted, for example, is briefly, selectively and evenly heated so that it expands. this creates enough space in the tool holder to insert the tool. when it cools down, the material of the holder contracts again evenly from all sides. in this way, the tool is clamped with high rigidity, maximum clamping force and centered. top why are special shrink fit chucks needed? special tool holders, shrink fit chucks, are usually used for shrinking. they are specially designed to retain their shape despite repeated heating and cooling. for example, they contain no moving parts so that their balancing quality is maintained; it is also important that the concentricity of the shrink fit chuck is also very high, otherwise even a very precisely centered tool is of no use. compared to conventional chucks, shrink chucks have the minor disadvantage that a separate chuck with a suitable diameter is required for each shank diameter. however, this is offset by the significantly higher concentricity, which is of great importance for high-quality machined workpieces. top what is a shrinking machine and how does it work? a shrink-fit machine heats the shrink-fit chuck, the tool holder, evenly in a short time using inductive current (i.e. via a magnetic field). with the appropriate tools and measuring devices, it then not only ensures that the new tool is inserted precisely centered, it can also ensure suitable length accuracy and measure and, if necessary, correct this before the controlled cooling of the shrink fit chuck. appropriate sensors also prevent the shrink fit chuck or tool from overheating. automated shrink technology ensures, for example, that the projection length and all other parameters that are important for processing the workpieces are automatically measured and correctly set - and that the tool is still available again within a very short time. this ensures short set-up times and lower costs overall. good shrink fit machines also have their own cooling unit in which the shrink fit chuck is evenly cooled. for example, contact cooling is used, some devices also wor
